story.title: Trial Set for Singer D4vd in Murder of 14-Year-Old Celeste Rivas Hernandez
story.summary: Singer D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, has been ordered to stand trial for the murder of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege that he dismembered her body, which was found in a Tesla registered to him. The trial follows a judge's ruling that sufficient evidence exists to proceed with the case.

explore_lenses.label: What evidence cleared the case for trial?
explore_lenses.title: The judge found probable cause, not guilt
explore_lenses.summary: The preliminary-hearing ruling means the prosecution presented enough evidence to continue the case; it does not resolve whether Burke is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

claims.text: Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Charlaine F. Olmedo ordered Burke to stand trial after a five-day preliminary hearing in which the prosecution called 12 witnesses.

A police DNA specialist testified that samples from apparent blood stains on items in Burke's garage strongly matched Rivas Hernandez; this was testimony offered by the prosecution, not a final jury finding.

Prosecutors also presented a theory linking alleged online purchases of a shovel, chainsaws, a body bag and an inflatable pool to the alleged dismemberment; the district attorney says blue plastic fragments found in the remains matched the type of pool Burke allegedly bought.

explore_lenses.label: How does Burke contest the prosecution's account?
explore_lenses.title: The defense disputes causation and the timeline
explore_lenses.summary: Burke has pleaded not guilty. His lawyers contest the claim that he caused Rivas Hernandez's death and have highlighted gaps in direct evidence of the alleged killing.

claims.text: Burke's attorneys stated that the evidence will show he did not murder Rivas Hernandez and was not the cause of her death; ABC reported that the defense says it will vigorously defend his innocence.

At the hearing, defense questioning established that no witness saw Rivas Hernandez enter Burke's home and no camera captured either her entry or Burke at the home during the prosecution's alleged killing window.

Prosecutors' competing account is that Rivas Hernandez's phone stopped transmitting after she arrived at Burke's home and that later messages from Burke were cover for a killing; that is an allegation prosecutors must prove at trial.

explore_lenses.label: What happens before any trial begins?
explore_lenses.title: An August 31 arraignment is the next listed hearing
explore_lenses.summary: The next publicly identified court date is a post-preliminary arraignment, when the case proceeds formally after the judge's ruling. No trial date is identified in the district attorney's July 27 announcement.

claims.text: The Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office says Burke is scheduled for a post-preliminary arraignment on August 31, 2026, in Department 105 of the Foltz Criminal Justice Center.

The charges listed by the district attorney are murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and unlawful mutilation of human remains, with special-circumstance and weapon allegations; the office expressly notes that all charges are allegations and that Burke is presumed innocent.
Forecast: the district attorney's office says a decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made later; if convicted as charged, it says Burke could face death or life without parole.

related_stories.title: Shooting at Seattle Food Festival Leaves Three Dead and Multiple Injured
related_stories.summary: A shooting at a food festival in Seattle resulted in the deaths of three individuals, with four others injured, including a two-year-old boy. Authorities have indicated that the incident may be gang-related. One suspect is in custody, while another remains at large as investigations continue.

related_stories.title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Stolen Unreleased Music and Content
related_stories.summary: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against unidentified hackers who allegedly stole her unreleased music, photos, and videos. In her complaint, she claims that the breach has caused 'irreparable harm' to her career and is seeking a court order to compel internet providers to reveal the hackers' identities.

related_stories.title: Bryan Kohberger Seeks to Withdraw Guilty Plea in Idaho Student Murders
related_stories.summary: Bryan Kohberger, who pleaded guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students in 2022, is now seeking to withdraw his guilty plea. This request follows his admission as part of a plea deal, and he is aiming to go to trial instead. Kohberger has filed a petition for post-conviction relief regarding his conviction.

related_stories.title: Gunfire Targets US Consulate in Toronto Again This Year
related_stories.summary: Shots were fired at the US consulate in Toronto, marking the second incident of this nature this year. Police engaged in a high-speed chase but did not apprehend the suspect, who remains at large. This follows a similar attack in June, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals.
